title: SettingsClient.status / ipfsDesktop.agentSettings.status
description: Messages of the SettingsClient.status() method (agent-settings-contract task 1.5). It reports transport and management state, not settings values: on the Desktop bridge (IPC channel ipfsDesktop.agentSettings.status) it is what lets the settings page show 'Managed by IPFS Desktop' with the running state and port (assessment-ui 5.5) and hide the manual endpoint and token fields; on HTTP it reports the cloud transport with no sidecar. It also carries the client-tracked applied record: the server applies synchronously and keeps no apply history, and the only history the UI shows is 'last applied by this browser/Desktop' (assessment-ui 5.3), so each SettingsClient implementation records the outcome of its own mutations.

StatusRequest.description: Empty payload. The channel takes no arguments.

transport.description: Which SettingsClient implementation answered. The provider (assessment-ui 5.6) is the only place that knows the transport; the page branches on managed_by_desktop, never on this value's string.

managed_by_desktop.description: True on the Desktop bridge: endpoint and secrets are managed in the main process, the manual endpoint and token fields are hidden, and the page shows 'Managed by IPFS Desktop' (assessment-ui 5.5). False on HTTP.

endpoint.description: The loopback sidecar endpoint ('Local endpoint, managed by Desktop :PORT', assessment-ui 5.1 item 5). Present only on the Desktop bridge while the sidecar runs. Always loopback; the bridge never exposes a remote endpoint here.

running.description: Whether the ipfs mcp sidecar process is running (desktop-mcp-sidecar 1.1).

port.description: The loopback port the sidecar bound (desktop-mcp-sidecar 1.2: 5050 preferred, else a free loopback port, never a silent fallback). Present when running is true.

sidecar.description: Sidecar state. Present only on the Desktop bridge. When the port changes the main process recreates the window (desktop-agent-settings-bridge 1.2), so the renderer never needs to re-read a stale endpoint.

revision.description: The settings revision the implementation last observed, when it has read the settings route. Lets the page detect that a get() would return newer state.

at.description: When the last mutation through this client finished, mapping assessment-ui 5.2 applied.at.

ok.description: Whether that mutation applied cleanly, mapping applied.ok. On failure the previous settings stayed in effect ('Nothing was changed. The previous backend is still in use.', assessment-ui 5.3).

error.description: Why the last mutation failed when ok is false, mapping applied.error. Never includes credentials or key material.

AppliedRecord.description: The last apply attempted through this client, tracked by the implementation itself. Absent before the first mutation. The server deliberately keeps no apply history; this is the only history the UI shows (assessment-ui 5.3).
